meta.title: Phosphor — Modern ANSI & ASCII Art Editor
meta.description: Turn images into ANSI or ASCII art in your browser, then paint, type, animate, and export.

app.noscript: Phosphor needs JavaScript enabled to run.

about.label: About Phosphor
about.tagline: Turn images into ANSI and ASCII, then keep drawing … with style.
about.p1: Phosphor began in 2019 as a small experiment to build tooling for a concept I called “ANSI Nouveau.” At the time, I was interested in the idea of recreating the mid-90s BBS experience I grew up with, but through a modern, high-fidelity lens. Like many passion projects, life got in the way and it eventually landed on the shelf.
about.p2: Years later, I came across a fantastic {moebiusFork} that added 256-color and full-color support. It reminded me of this project, so I dragged it out of storage, dusted off the code—and leveraging modern tools and techniques, brought it back to life.
about.moebiusForkLink: fork of the Moebius ANSI editor
about.p3: Phosphor started as an image-to-ANSI converter, and today it brings two workflows together. It turns images into ANSI or ASCII that you can fine-tune to your liking, then lets you draw and type over that cell by cell and export as .ans or .utf8ans. Finish your piece here, or take the file into another editor for a final pass—whether you're after “Pure ANSI” or the full-color, UTF-8 “ANSI Nouveau” modern style that inspired the project.
about.p4: It's still early days. Expect rough edges on phones and small tablets—though iPad with Apple Pencil works well in testing. Feedback, bug reports, and ideas are always welcome: open an issue on {github}, or fork the repo and take it in your own direction.
about.creditErtdfgcvb: {ertdfgcvb} (Andreas Gysin) for the inspiration for Phosphor with the (awesome) {playCore} library
about.creditMoebius: Andy Herbert, Blocktronics and MeaTLoTioN for their work on Moebius
about.creditDurdraw: cmang for {durdraw}, the ANSI and ASCII art editor that animates
about.credit16Colors: lordscarlet (Doug Moore) and Brendan O'Connor for creating sixteencolors and those working to keep {sixteenColors} alive today.
about.creditFonts: The fonts: {ibmVga} from VileR's Ultimate Oldschool PC Font Pack ({ccBySa}), {jetbrains} by The JetBrains Mono Project Authors ({ofl1}), {unscii} by viznut (public domain), and {unifont} by Roman Czyborra, Paul Hardy and others ({ofl2})
about.creditIcons: The icons: most are from {fontAwesome} by Fonticons, Inc. ({ccBy})
about.creditScene: And the many authors, maintainers, and ANSI artists who have inspired me over the years—too many to name
about.thanks: Thanks to all of you for the inspiration, and for keeping the scene going.

cols.label: Dimensions
cols.help: Canvas width in columns and height in pixel rows (two pixel rows make one character row).

renderStyle.help: ANSI colors each character and its background. Color ASCII draws colored characters on black, using denser glyphs for stronger colors. Monochrome ASCII uses one color, mapping brightness from light to dense.

chars.help: Characters the converter chooses from—randomly for ANSI, or from dark to bright for ASCII. Repeat a character to weight it higher. Best match and By shape ignore repeats.

seed.help: Controls random character placement in ANSI mode. Same seed, same pattern—roll the dice to shuffle.

quantize.help: Full color keeps 24-bit color. VGA and CGA snap to classic 256- and 16-color palettes. Limited count picks the best N colors from the image, and Custom color list uses only the hex colors you enter.

ditherStyle.help: How dithering mixes the palette's colors. Floyd–Steinberg scatters them like grain; Ordered lays them in a regular crosshatch that stays put from frame to frame.

dither.label: Dither
dither.help: Mixes the palette's colors in a fine pattern where the picture falls between them, so gradients come out smooth instead of in bands. Paint keeps its own color. With Best match or By shape, the characters carry it from cell to cell.

smoothing.help: Controls how the image is sampled onto the grid. High blends smoothly; Low preserves sharp edges and grain.

colorizeStrength.label: Colorize
colorizeStrength.help: Tints the image toward a single hue while preserving light and shadow.

hue.label: Hue shift
hue.help: Rotates every color around the color wheel.

invert.label: Invert
invert.help: Flips colors to their negatives (applied after Colorize and Hue shift).

brightness.label: Brightness
brightness.help: Shifts the overall image lighter or darker.

contrast.label: Contrast
contrast.help: Pushes lights and darks further apart, or brings them closer.

levelsBlack.label: Black point
levelsBlack.help: Tones at or below this become black, and the rest spread out to fill the range.

levelsWhite.label: White point
levelsWhite.help: Tones at or above this become white, and the rest spread out to fill the range.

levelsMid.label: Midtones
levelsMid.help: Lifts the middle tones (above 1) or deepens them (below 1) without moving black or white.

saturation.label: Saturation
saturation.help: Boosts color intensity or pulls it toward grayscale.

posterize.label: Posterize
posterize.help: Cuts each color channel to this many steps, for flat, poster-like color.

threshold.label: Threshold
threshold.help: Splits the picture in two: tones at or above this level take the light color, the rest the dark one.

blur.label: Blur
blur.help: Softens noise and fine grain before the picture is converted. Applied before the other effects.

flatten.label: Flatten
flatten.help: Groups nearby tones into clean, painterly shapes.

sharpen.label: Sharpen
sharpen.help: Crisps up edges and fine detail.

edges.label: Edges
edges.help: Traces detected outlines in your chosen edge color.

edgeThickness.label: Edge thickness
edgeThickness.help: Controls how bold the traced outlines appear.

charChoice.help: Random picks from your set by the seed. Best match picks the character and its two palette colors that come closest to the picture. By shape compares each character's shape with the picture's detail in the cell.

charChoiceAscii.help: By intensity (Color ASCII) and By brightness (Monochrome ASCII) pick a character further along your set the brighter the cell. By shape compares each character's shape with the picture's detail in the cell.

solids.label: Solids
solids.help: How strongly a plain solid cell is preferred over a shade or a half-block.

patternLight.label: Pattern light
patternLight.help: How a character's ink mixes its two colors: 0% is a plain average, 100% mixes them as light does on a screen, so shades read lighter.

font.label: Font
font.help: Sets the display font for your canvas. Use Load font to add a monospaced TrueType, OpenType, or WOFF font from your computer. Bitmap fonts look crispest at multiples of their native size (16 or 32px for 8×16 fonts). Your font choice stays in this browser; in a shared room, you'll see the host's font temporarily.

consent.title: Before you open SOCIAL
consent.intro: SOCIAL lets you watch people draw live, draw together, or host your own room. Here's how your privacy works.
consent.lobbyBody: Opening SOCIAL connects your browser to our server. People in the lobby can see your username (guests get a random three-word nickname). Public rooms show their host, title, viewer count, and a live preview.
consent.joiningBody: Your browser connects directly to the host's, so each of you can see the other's IP address. That can reveal your approximate location and internet provider, so use a VPN if you want to hide it. Chat goes through the host's browser, and anyone in the room can see and copy it.
consent.startingBody: The people you admit see your art as you draw it, and everyone who joins can see your IP address. Public rooms show a preview in the lobby. Anyone you invite to draw gets the whole project, including the original image. If someone reports your room, we keep a snapshot of the canvas to review and resolve the report.
consent.beKindBody: Don't bully, harass, threaten anyone, or attack people for who they are. Don't use someone's IP address against them or share their personal information. Keep public rooms appropriate, respect other people's art, and only report in good faith. Hosts can remove or block people, and anyone signed in with a confirmed email can report a person or room.
